title: Ishaan Khatter Is the Only Indian on the Biarritz Film Festival Jury. Kristen Stewart Is Chairing It.
excerpt: The actor joins a seven-member international panel at the French festival dedicated to emerging voices in cinema. It's another marker in a quiet but steady global pivot.
body:
Ishaan Khatter has been invited to serve on the jury of the Biarritz Film Festival — Nouvelles Vagues 2026, which runs from June 23 to 28 in the south of France. He is the only Indian on the panel. Kristen Stewart is chairing it.

The seven-member jury also includes Canadian actress Whitney Peak, French actor-director Raphaël Quenard, French filmmaker Nathan Ambrosioni, actress Suzy Bemba, Italian director Carolina Cavalli, and British actress Esmé Creed-Miles. The festival, now in its fourth edition, focuses on cinema centered around younger generations and emerging voices — a mandate that has made it one of Europe's more closely watched indie platforms.

## A Quiet Global Pivot

For the Indian diaspora watching Ishaan Khatter's career trajectory, this is a familiar pattern playing out in an unfamiliar way. Most Bollywood actors who "go global" do it through Hollywood casting calls or Netflix partnerships. Ishaan's path has been different — slower, more lateral, more rooted in the festival circuit.

His performance in Mira Nair's *A Suitable Boy* introduced him to international audiences. *The Royals* expanded that footprint. His most recent project, *Homebound*, has drawn appreciation in festival and critical circles. None of these are the kind of projects that dominate box office weekends in India, but they've built a particular kind of credibility — the kind that gets you invited to judge films alongside Kristen Stewart in Biarritz.

## The Gold House Connection

Earlier this year, Ishaan featured on the Gold House Gold 100 list, becoming the only Indian male actor on the annual lineup that recognizes influential Asian and Pacific figures across industries. The Gold House list carries weight in the Asian American community — it's the same organization behind the Gold Gala and the Gold Open initiative that drives opening-weekend box office campaigns for Asian-led films.

For NRIs in the US, this kind of recognition matters differently than a ₹300 crore opening weekend. It signals that Indian talent is being taken seriously in spaces that weren't designed for them.

## What's Next

On the work front, Ishaan will next appear in *Jugaadu*, a comic caper that also marks his first venture as a producer. He shared his first look from the film on Instagram earlier this month.

The Biarritz invitation isn't the kind of headline that trends on social media for more than an afternoon. But it's the kind of career move that compounds — each international engagement opening a door to the next. For a 27-year-old actor from Mumbai, sitting on a jury chaired by Kristen Stewart in a French coastal town isn't the destination. It's the signal.
author: Diaspora Desk
